newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen choppy at open, eye on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen choppy at open, eye on FOMC.

--------------------MARKET COMMENT---------------------------- * Toronto stocks were expected to face choppy trade at the open, as the market tries to catch up after the Canadian holiday Monday. * Overall trade seen quiet ahead of FOMC.

Toronto stocks were expected to face choppy trade at the open on Tuesday as the market tries to catch up after Canada's holiday Monday, but analysts said dealings would be light ahead of this afternoon's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.

"We've got mixed factors that are going to try to pull the TSE in different directions, so I think we're going to have a choppy and pretty quiet morning," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said Toronto stocks may try to play catch up after New York stocks gained some ground on Monday.
But Beattie said Canadian bonds remained under pressure and the recovery in gold prices was not enough to lift the sector out of its recent downtrend.
"And most important of all, this is Fed day... and I suspect trading is going to be very quiet this morning ahead of the Fed announcement," Beattie said.

The FOMC, the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy arm, begins meeting at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT to discuss U.S. interest rates. Economists are divided as to whether it will take action against inflation by raising the federal funds rate.
The FOMC verdict is expected at about 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
On Friday, the Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slid 29.27 points to 6247.38.

In economic news, Canada's wholesale trade fell 2.7 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in march from February to C$22.46 billion. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 1.2 percent month-on-month rise in March.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* The murky legal battle over the ownership of two gold concessions at Placer Dome Inc's Las Cristinas property in Venezuela has thickened. Crystallex International Corp said on Monday the Supreme Court of Venezuela had confirmed the validity of the transfer of the concessions to Crystallex's Venezuelan unit, Inversora Mael CA. Despite the ruling, certain officials of the Ministery of Energy and Mines are continuing to deny Mael's ownership of the concessions. Placer Dome has stated its ownership is certain.

* BC Sugar Refinery Ltd said it agreed to a C$14.75 per share takeover bid by Great Pacific Acquisition Inc. It said the deal is conditional on having 50.1 percent of BC Sugar's common shares tendered to the offer. An affiliate of Great Pacific already holds 28.41 percent of common shares.
